faq.q1: How do I add a book?
faq.q1.a1: First and foremost, search for both the author and the title of the book to avoid creating duplicates.
faq.q1.a2: If a Work and an Edition containing it exist, the questions below will help you decide whether to create a new Edition.
faq.q1.a3: Otherwise, here is a step-by-step procedure:
faq.q1.step2Post: Work with a relationship to the Author
faq.q1.step2Pre: On the Author page, click on 'Add Work' to create a
faq.q1.step3Mid: Edition with a relationship to the Work.
faq.q1.step3Pre: On the Work page, click 'Add Edition' to create an
faq.q1.step3Sub1Post: Edition Group will be created automatically, but you can select an existing one
faq.q1.step3Sub2Post: Publisher if you cannot find an existing one
faq.q1.step4: To enter another format of the same book (see explanations below), go to the Edition Group and click the 'Add Edition' button. Repeat step 4.
faq.q2: When should I create a new Edition of a Work?
faq.q2.item1: When it is published in a different format (e.g. paperback and e-book)
faq.q2.item2: When there are substantial content (textual or editorial) changes
faq.q2.item3: Translations will both be a new Work and a new Edition for it.
faq.q2.item4: Add a relationship between the original and the translated Works
faq.q2.item5: New cover or changed credits/attribution on the cover
faq.q3: When should I not create a new Edition of a Work?
faq.q3.item1: Minimal changes as in proofreading errors
faq.q3.item3: Reprints of the same Edition. You can mention “Reprint – [date]” in the annotations.
faq.q3.item4: When the edition uses the same ISBN (with rare exceptions)
faq.q4: When should two Editions be part of the same Edition Group?
faq.q4.introPre: Edition Groups exist to group together all the variations of an edition (an identifiable set of works) in a given language. Here are examples of Editions that should be part of the same Edition Group:
faq.q4.item1: Different formats of the same edition (paperback, hardcover and e-book by the same publisher)
faq.q4.item5: Co-editions (same book published in different countries by different publishers)

help.authorDesc: – an individual, group or collective that participates in the creative process of an artistic work. It also includes translators, illustrators, editors, etc.
help.editionDesc: – a published physical or digital version of one or more Works.
help.editionExamples: Examples: book, anthology, comic book, magazine, leaflet
help.editionGroupDesc: – a logical grouping of different Editions of the same book.
help.editionGroupExamples: Example: paperback, hardcover and e-book editions of a novel
help.editionNote: Note: An Author can self-publish an Edition
help.entitiesDescription: Entities are the main concepts used to describe a bibliographic record through their relationships

help.examplesIntro: The following examples should help you understand the different entities and how they relate to each other:
help.glossaryAliasesDesc: – Variant names for an entity such as alternate spelling, different script, stylistic representation, acronyms, etc.
help.glossaryAliasesExampleName1: Name: 村上 春樹 – Alias (english): Haruki Murakami
help.glossaryAliasesExampleName2: Name: bell hooks - Alias (full name): Gloria Jean Watkins
help.glossaryAuthorCreditsDesc: – As appearing on the publication cover. For example, if the author is using a pseudonym, the credits should reflect that.
help.glossaryDisambiguationDesc: – Short comment added to differentiate between similarly-named entities.
help.glossaryDisambiguationExample1: The Alchemist (philosophical novel) by Paulo Coelho
help.glossaryDisambiguationExample2: The Alchemyst (YA novel featuring Nicolas Flamel) by Michael Scott
help.glossaryEntitiesDesc: – Conceptual items representing the various authors and parts of a publication. See the previous Entities section for details.
help.glossaryFormatDesc: – Refers to different printing and/or binding methods, or digital distribution. For example: paperback, mass-market, hardcover and e-book are all book formats
help.glossaryIdentifiersDescPost: When adding identifiers to an entity, you can enter either the identifier only (Q2517049) or a full link (https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q2517049).
help.glossaryIdentifiersDescPre: – identity of an entity in other databases and services, such as ISBN, barcode, MusicBrainz ID, WikiData ID, etc.
help.glossaryIntro: Here is a short description of some of the main terms you will encounter. Some terms are borrowed from MusicBrainz; click on the term to be redirected to the MusicBrainz guidelines or a definition.
help.glossaryPrintingDescPost: One edition of a work may have any number of printings, e. g. a same Edition can have a first impression and a second impression.
help.glossaryPrintingDescPre: – A batch of identical copies of an edition of a work that is printed in a same, single production set-up.
help.glossarySortNameDesc: – Modified name to help sorting alphabetically
help.glossarySortNameExample2: A Tale of Two Cities -> Tale of Two Cities, A
help.glossarySortNameExample3: Benito Pérez Galdós -> Pérez Galdós, Benito

help.workDesc: – a distinct intellectual or artistic creation expressed in words and/or images. Here we are not talking, for example, about a physical book, but the introduction, story, illustrations, etc. it contains.
help.workExamples: Examples: novel, poem, translation, introduction & foreword, article, research paper, etc.
